corpusSummary: Across a broad collection of 2026 social-science records, this corpus charts how large language models intersect with human activity in cognition, governance, education, health, and policy. It highlights themes of embodiment limits, trust and governance, AI-enabled learning, health information risk, and the use of LLMs as research tools, while noting safety, ethics, and equity considerations and the persistent gaps between algorithmic and situated knowledge.

themes.name: Cognition, embodiment, and epistemic boundaries
themes.description: Explores how LLM cognition relates to embodied human meaning, highlighting limits in sense-making and risks of anthropomorphism.

themes.name: Trust, governance, and adoption of AI
themes.description: Investigates how organizations and individuals build trust, govern, and adopt generative AI across work, health, and civic contexts.

themes.name: AI-enabled education and learning ecosystems
themes.description: Examines AI-assisted teaching, scaffolding, tutoring, and assessment across diverse learning settings and populations.

themes.name: AI in health, risk communication, and patient education
themes.description: Assesses AI's role in health information, patient education, and clinical decision support with safety and equity considerations.
